# 7.3 · Retry and Budget

`Level 7: Agents Without Magic` · `+25 XP` · `drill 3 of 3`

## The job
Write the guardrails around flaky, metered calls. `retry(fn, attempts, base_delay, sleep,
retry_on, max_delay)` calls `fn()` until it succeeds, sleeping base_delay * 2^i (capped at
max_delay) between attempts, and re-raises the last error when out of attempts. Errors not
in `retry_on` propagate immediately. `TokenBudget` tracks spending and raises
`BudgetExceeded` before going over. `guarded_call` charges the budget for every attempt.

## Why it matters
APIs time out and rate-limit; retrying with backoff is mandatory. But each retry costs as
much as the first try, and an agent that retries inside a loop can quietly multiply your
bill. Charging before the call and refusing to overspend is the difference between a
surprising invoice and a clear error message.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 7.3     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 7.3      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Take `sleep` as a parameter so tests can pass a fake that records delays instead of waiting.
2. Delay before retry number i (counting from 0) is min(max_delay, base_delay * 2 ** i). There is no sleep after the final failure.
3. Only catch the exception types in `retry_on`; anything else should escape on the first attempt.
4. `charge` checks first and only then adds, so a rejected charge leaves `used` unchanged.
5. In `guarded_call`, BudgetExceeded is not retryable: retrying will not make money appear.

</details>
